slides.heading: Union Find
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Famous Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Union Find, a medium famous algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Disjoint-set with createSet, find (null if unknown) and union, using path compression and union by rank.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Disjoint-set with createSet, find (null if unknown) and union, using path compression and union by rank.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each set is a tree with a representative root; path compression and union by rank keep trees flat.
slides.narration: Each set is a tree with a representative root; path compression and union by rank keep trees flat.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Naive: label every element with its set ID → union is O(n)
Plain parent trees → find can be O(n)
Rank + path compression → nearly O(1) amortised (α(n))
slides.narration: Storing a set ID per element makes union linear, since you relabel a whole set. Parent pointers make union cheap, but trees can become long chains. Union by rank plus path compression keeps operations effectively constant, inverse-Ackermann time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. find follows parents with path compression
3. union attaches the shorter tree under the taller
slides.narration: Step by step. First, createSet makes a single-node tree. Second, find follows parents with path compression. Third, union attaches the shorter tree under the taller.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: createSet(0…4): every node is its own root
slides.narration: Create five sets. Every node is its own parent, so each is a root.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: union(0, 1): roots 0, 1 → attach by rank
slides.narration: Union 0 and 1: their roots are 0 and 1. Equal ranks, so the second root goes under the first and its rank grows.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: union(2, 3): roots 2, 3 → attach by rank
slides.narration: Union 2 and 3: their roots are 2 and 3. Equal ranks, so the second root goes under the first and its rank grows.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: union(0, 3): roots 0, 2 → attach by rank
slides.narration: Union 0 and 3: their roots are 0 and 2. Equal ranks, so the second root goes under the first and its rank grows.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: find(3) → 0 with path compression
slides.narration: Finding three walks up to the root, zero, and compresses the path so three points straight at zero next time.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Create set makes a node its own parent with rank zero. Find recursively finds the root and rewrites the parent pointer to it, which is path compression. Union finds both roots and attaches the lower-rank root under the higher one, bumping rank on ties.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is about O of alpha(n) amortised per op. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: find on an unknown value → null
Union of the same set → no-op
slides.narration: Return null for unknown values, and make union a no-op when both are already in the same set.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Used in Kruskal's MST and connectivity queries
Follow-up: union by size; count components
slides.narration: Union-find powers Kruskal's algorithm and dynamic connectivity. Union by size works as well as rank.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Each set is a tree with a representative root; path compression and union by rank keep trees flat.
slides.narration: To recap Union Find: Each set is a tree with a representative root; path compression and union by rank keep trees flat. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
